simple.meaning: יַבֵּל (yabbêl) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “having running sores.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 1 time across Leviticus, beginning at Leviticus 22:22. Its contexts include offering, altar.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יַבֵּל (H2990).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: יַבֵּל (yabbêl) / H2990 is traced through Leviticus 22:22 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: You shall not offer what is blind, is injured, is maimed, has a wart, is festering, or has a running sore to Yahweh, nor make an offering by fire of them on the altar to Yahweh.
